title: Creating a theatre show with live actors and animated characters — where to start?
author: Puzzleheaded-River45
selftext:
I’m looking into creating a children’s theatre show that mixes live actors with animated characters on a screen. Basically, characters that can talk, move and interact with the performers onstage.

I’m a musician/producer and fairly tech-savvy, but I’ve no real animation experience.  
I’ve been messing around with AI-generated 3D models, Three.js and HTML animation, but I’m wondering what the best way to approach something like this would be.  
Ideally I’d like decent-quality 3D characters with facial expressions, lip-sync and movement, without having to animate absolutely everything by hand.  
Is this realistic for someone who’s not an animator? Would Blender, Unreal, iClone or something else be the way to go? And would you use pre-rendered animation or something running in real time?

Would love to hear from anyone who’s done something similar or has suggestions for a good workflow!

comments.author: Natural-Comedian6670
comments.body:
Ensure it’s entertaining without any tech .. the script etc should be priority   
You could probably get stylized cartoonish heads working more easily with camera / face tracking , I’ve seen YouTubers / twitch avatars that work in realtime from a laptop camera and unity ( I think it was ) .. actors would be backstage and it could all be realtime . 

There’s a team doing great looking puppets in unreal but that would be a hard tech challenge unless you are animation / tech artist : unreal expert .

replies.author: Puzzleheaded-River45
replies.body:
Thanks! Yeah the script and show side of it is all in hand, I have lots of experience and infrastructure there, it’s just the actual graphics side of it, I am very out of touch about what people are doing in those areas.

That’s a great idea about face tracking, unfortunately cast is to be kept very small as children’s show ticket prices are a lot smaller

replies.author: Natural-Comedian6670
replies.body:
it would just be someone sat infront of a laptop camea... no face markers or anything clever. .. not too different to those cat faces you mightve seen on a zoom call . (well, better than that...)..

i assume as long as someone has a face, it would work. you just setup the poses for vowels/ words , expressions etc , its not full facial animation to an audio track. 

you could probably but some sound activated motors in a plant pot and it could give them impression the plant is 'talking' with pre recorded audio from an mp3 player.

ask claude / an ai , it could probably help identify solutioms or even come up with one if you have the tokens.
